Manufactured by [[Neuro-Saav Corporation]], the '''TD2.3 [[Electrobinoculars/Legends|electrobinoculars]]''' consisted of stereoscopic sights and a computer-enhanced magnification systems encased in a weatherproof plastic shell. It also included imaging chips that allowed use during bright days or dark nights. Another component was the automated dampener filter that provided protection against [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] flashes, [[Flash grenade/Legends|flash grenades]] or other sudden bursts of light. The TD2.3 could focus on targets up to 600 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] away.

==Characteristics==
[[File:At-at.png|thumb|left|200px|Advancing [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-AT]] sighting using TD2.3 electrobinoculars.]]
The Model TD2.3 was a type of [[Electrobinoculars/Legends|electrobinoculars]] manufactured by [[Neuro-Saav Corporation|Neuro-Saav]]. Like all electrobinoculars, the TD2.3 employed stereoscopic sights and [[Computer/Legends|computer]]-enhanced magnification to view objects at long ranges.<ref name="EGWT" /> Encased in a durable, weatherproof [[Plastic/Legends|plastic]] shell,<ref name="NEGWT" /> the unit had three individual lenses that worked in concert; the image balance lens, the electronic lens, and the manual magnification scope. Users looked through the electrobinocular's twin viewing scopes to see the image gathered by the lenses on an internal display screen.<ref name="EGWT" />

The TD2.3 had computer-enhanced [[Telescope/Legends|telescopic]] lenses that gave the electrobinoculars a magnification factor of five hundred. [[Imaging chip]]s were used to adjust and enhance the available visible light,<ref name="EGWT" /> allowing the viewer to see clear images even on the brightest day<ref name="NEGWT" /> or in low-light conditions and totally dark environments. Dampener filters were installed in the TD2.3 that would engage automatically if bursts of light were detected, such as those from [[Flash grenade/Legends|flash-bang grenades]], [[spot-luma]]s,<ref name="EGWT" /> [[Blaster/Legends|blasterfire]], or [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheric]] phenomenon,<ref name="NEGWT" /> to prevent the user from being blinded.<ref name="EGWT" />

[[File:ModelTD2-3electrobinoculars-TCVD.jpg|thumb|right|180px|TD2.3's with case.]]
A secondary nonelectronic lens was capable of one hundred times magnification and was used if the electronic lens failed or if it was returning readings that were considered to be unreliable. The TD2.3 featured an instant-focus function that could quickly shift between objects that were at different distances<ref name="EGWT" /> as well as providing a high-resolution image even when the target was moving.<ref name="NEGWT" /> On-screen readouts would display the distance to the object, as well as the elevation, and the relative and true azimuths.<ref name="EGWT" /> An internal computer would analyze all of the information gathered by the electrobinoculars, automatically sharpening and enhancing images as well as employing wide and zoom angles.<ref name="NEGWT" />

Dials and controls on the left hand side of the electrobinoculars were used to activate the TD2.3's zoom function,<ref name="EGWT" /> focus the lenses,<ref name="NEGWT" /> and to adjust the low-light settings. Focus studs allowed for precise incremental adjustment of the telescopic magnification, while eight zoom settings could be preprogrammed into TD2.3 which could be cycled through by pressing the reset button. The TD2.3 could be run through a self-diagnostic routine<ref name="EGWT" /> that was intended to ensure that the electronic imagers provided a constant and clear reception,<ref name="NEGWT" /> which was activated when the calibration switch was pressed.<ref name="EGWT" />

The TD2.3 had several [[Dataport/Legends|dataports]] that could be used to link the electrobinoculars to peripheral devices such as [[Holorecorder/Legends|holorecorders]], [[Datapad/Legends|datapads]], and [[recording rod]]s. Internal software allowed the device to be synchronized with [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], displaying an electronically generated crosshairs on the readout screens.<ref name="EGWT" /> The unit's [[Power cell/Legends|power cells]] charged themselves and lasted approximately six [[Standard month/Legends|months]].<ref name="NEGWT" />

==Behind the scenes==
In ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' and its sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]'', the Model TD2.3 was depicted as the symbol for the integrated rangefinder, with an AT-AT in its field of view, which increased infantry range to its final level.
